summary: The study investigates the scalability of plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposited ruthenium films for interconnect applications. Ruthenium films were deposited using MethylCyclopentadienylPyrrolylRuthenium (MeCpPy)Ru and N2/NH3 plasma on titanium nitride (TiN) and tantalum nitride (TaN) substrates. The growth characteristics, layer continuity, and conformality of the Ru films on scaled metal nitride layers were evaluated. The results show that the thickness of the metal nitride can be reduced without affecting Ru growth, and the conformality of the Ru layer in narrow line structures is maintained. The study highlights the importance of minimizing the thickness of the metal nitride layer to enable future interconnect applications.
evidence: Ru thin films were deposited by plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition using MethylCyclopentadienylPyrrolylRuthenium (MeCpPy)Ru and N2/NH3 plasma. The growth characteristics have been studied on titanium nitride or tantalum nitride substrates of various thicknesses. The scalability of the metal nitride layer is crucial for future interconnect applications.
